long_biography.plain_text:
Central Car Parks began with a practical use for London's post-war bomb sites. Gosling and Ronald Hobson converted vacant land into paid parking, then acquired National Car Parks and built a business positioned for rising car ownership. Its nationwide network and related roadside-assistance interests made car-parking services the foundation of Gosling's fortune before the partners sold the group in 1998.

Naval service remained the other durable institution in his life. Gosling had joined the Royal Navy as a teenager and served in HMS Leander during the Second World War. In retirement he channelled business proceeds into naval personnel, charities and heritage, notably through the Gosling Foundation. His honorary vice-admiral rank recognised that sustained service and support.

uncertainties.detail: Gosling sold National Car Parks in 1998, and no complete public balance sheet establishes a different dominant private industry at his death. Service is retained at high confidence because car parking remained the only strongly documented principal business and wealth foundation; charitable foundation investments are not treated as his private operating industry.

The documented launch followed wartime service and trainee-surveyor work, with a modest initial parking venture on vacant London land. Together with the recorded non-business parental background, this positively supports an independent start without implying an absence of all ordinary support.

The available memorial source identifies Lambeth as the registration district, not unequivocally as the place of birth. No birthplace proposal is made. Companies House and complementary records do support the proposed birth date fields.

The dossier attributes the fortune to paid car-parking services. Gosling Foundation grants, Royal Navy support and maritime-heritage work are treated as later uses of business proceeds, while his honorary vice-admiral rank is described only as recognition of that service.

The existing Wikipedia link matches the exact owner. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, Facebook, X, YouTube or TikTok account met the identity threshold; only the canonical NCP company website is proposed.
